components.css: .ds-action{position:relative;isolation:isolate;overflow:hidden;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;min-height:52px;padding:14px 23px;font:700 .78rem Manrope,sans-serif;letter-spacing:.07em;text-decoration:none;border-radius:0;border:1px solid #d7dbe1;transition:color 220ms ease,background-color 320ms ease,border-color 220ms ease,transform 120ms cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)}.ds-action::before{content:"";position:absolute;inset:0;z-index:-1;background:#c4d3e6;transform:scaleX(0);transform-origin:left;transition:transform 320ms cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)}.ds-action-face{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:16px}.ds-action-clip{display:inline-block;overflow:hidden}.ds-action-label{display:inline-block;transition:transform 220ms cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)}.ds-action-arrow{width:18px;height:18px;flex:0 0 18px;transition:transform 220ms cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)}.ds-action:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #d4dfed;outline-offset:5px}.ds-action:focus-visible :is(.ds-action-label,.ds-action-arrow){transform:none;transition:none}@media(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine){.ds-action:hover::before{transform:scaleX(1)}.ds-action:hover{color:#101114;background:#c4d3e6}.ds-action:hover .ds-action-label{transform:translateY(-1px)}.ds-action:hover .ds-action-arrow{transform:translateX(4px)}}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-action,.ds-action::before,.ds-action-label,.ds-action-arrow{transition:none;transform:none}}.ds-action{background:#f1f2f4;color:#050505}

narrative.overview:
Nortivo's current local implementation uses an architectural black environment, condensed display lettering and silver controls. The incremental investment-technology extension retains this world while giving financial research, trading systems and the existing report a stronger presence. Manrope, restrained dividers and explicit feedback keep product, contact and support areas readable.

The system was extracted from the implemented website on 17 November 2026. The base extension is dist/assets/nortivo-engineered.css. The incremental financial presentation and interaction layer is dist/assets/investment-v2.css, with its behaviour in investment-v2.js. Earlier stylesheets remain inside the named nt-legacy cascade layer, preserving their layout and interaction foundations beneath the current visual rules. This document supersedes the older navy, blue-action and warm editorial public palettes.
keyCharacteristics: Obsidian and charcoal surfaces with occasional soft-white sections.
Self-hosted Barlow Condensed display text, Manrope interface text and IBM Plex Mono financial figures.
Asymmetric compositions, large real project previews and ruled service rows.
Flat operational workspaces, persistent field labels and readable status text.
Optional motion around marketing imagery, report charts and explicit control feedback.
Equivalent Norwegian Bokmål and English routes.
dos: Do use the current black, charcoal, silver and soft-white palette on Nortivo company surfaces.
Do reserve condensed uppercase display type for the public presentation hierarchy.
Do use Manrope for practical interfaces, labels, form content and data explanations.
Do use IBM Plex Mono for financial figures and preserve exact report definitions.
Do preserve bilingual navigation, visible focus, label associations and written states.
Do preserve supplied product assets, actual screenshots and clear demonstration status.
Do preserve existing functional contracts while extending their visual treatment.
Do keep generated-image provenance and font licence records with the project.
donts: Don't present earlier navy, blue-action or warm editorial tokens as the current public system.
Don't invent company achievements, customer evidence, product availability or connected services.
Don't conceal required content behind animation completion.
Don't add scroll hijacking, excessive glow, rainbow gradients or unnecessary 3D dependencies.
Don't use color as the only indicator of a state or financial result.
Don't turn the prescribed hero eyebrow into a default for unrelated sections.
Don't present reported historical results or simulated examples as audited, live or guaranteed outcomes.
Don't apply public cinematic motion to authentication or support tasks.
